record.original_question: Can we show that G is dense in Diff ω (S1 )0 ?

evidence.quote: Question 8.5. Can we show that G is dense in Diff ω (S1 )0 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R}) = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\{\pm I\}$ act on the circle $S^1$ by Möbius transformations, and set $G_1 := \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$, viewed as a topological group of real-analytic diffeomorphisms of $S^1$. For each integer $n \geq 1$, let $p_n \colon G_n \to G_1$ denote the $n$-fold cyclic connected covering of $G_1$; the group $G_n$ acts on $S^1$ as a group of real-analytic diffeomorphisms by lifting the action of $G_1$ through the $n$-fold cover $S^1 \to S^1$. Let $R_1 \subset G_1$ be the rotation subgroup (isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$) and set $R_n := p_n^{-1}(R_1)$, which is again isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For each $n \geq 1$ define
$$ G^{(n)} := G_1 \ast_{R_1} G_2 \ast_{R_2} \cdots \ast_{R_{n-1}} G_n,$$
the iterated amalgamated free product of $G_1, \ldots, G_n$ along the common rotation subgroup, realized as a subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)_0$ (the identity component of the group of orientation-preserving real-analytic diffeomorphisms of $S^1$). The natural inclusions $G^{(n)} \hookrightarrow G^{(n+1)}$ form a direct system, and we set
$$ G := \varinjlim_{n} G^{(n)} \;\subseteq\; \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)_0.$$
Equip $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)_0$ with its standard topology (uniform convergence of all derivatives on $S^1$, or equivalently the inductive-limit topology coming from real-analytic extensions to annular neighborhoods of $S^1$).

Question: Is $G$ dense in $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)_0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is attributed to Tsuboi and, as noted shortly after it was posed, was resolved by work of James Giblin and Vladimir Markovic on closed transitive subgroups of $\mathrm{Homeo}(S^1)$, which classifies such subgroups and implies the asserted density. Thus the question is regarded as solved in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: Classification of continuously transitive circle groups (Giblin–Markovic)
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of closed transitive subgroups of Homeo(S^1) containing a non-constant continuous path; the list is SO(2), PSL(2,R), PSL_k(2,R), Homeo_k(S^1), Homeo(S^1).
status_evidence.claim: Giblin–Markovic's classification of continuously transitive circle groups is the result cited as resolving the density question for G in Diff^ω(S^1)_0.

status_evidence.title: Problem list on Foliations and Diffeomorphism groups (HTML)
status_evidence.snippet: Just after posing this question, Michele Triestino told me that there is a paper by James Giblin and Vladimir Markovic ... which solved this question.
status_evidence.claim: The poser notes the question was solved by Giblin–Markovic.
